clue.text: Slam nobody else can make

parts.note: a slam is a harsh attack in words; the only one no other person can deliver is the one you aim at yourself

explanation.surface: A bridge player bids a slam that no rival could bring off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slam' tempts the bridge or tennis solver; here it is a verbal attack, and only the speaker can direct it inward.
explanation.definitionFit: Finding fault with one's own conduct is an attack that only its target can launch.

clue.text: A student of the occult? Darwin was

definitions.meaning: someone who studies ghosts, magic and things beyond the natural world
read as two words: Charles Darwin was a superb student of nature

explanation.surface: Was Darwin secretly dabbling in the occult?
explanation.definitionFit: Split as 'super naturalist' it praises a great biologist; as one word it names a believer in or student of the paranormal.

clue.text: Strong line taken in pedestrianised border town?

indicators.note: a pedestrianised town has had its cars removed, so the vehicle is taken out of the word

parts.note: Carlisle is the English city nearest the Scottish border

explanation.surface: A council closes the streets of a frontier town to traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: CARLISLE, a city in Cumbria close to the Scottish border, loses CAR because 'pedestrianised' streets have none.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a hard-wearing twisted cotton thread, used for stockings, so a strong thread or line.

clue.text: It takes time with a twisted leg to find a carriage

parts.note: a cabriole is a curved, S-shaped furniture leg

explanation.surface: Someone with a bad leg needs a ride in a carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: A cabriole is a furniture term: the curved leg of a Queen Anne chair, not an injured limb.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabriolet is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle with a folding hood.

clue.text: Nearly all abuse fashionable her-mone

definitions.note: the clue's spelling of hormone, playing on 'her' since the clue is a jokey coinage for a chemical messenger

indicators.note: nearly all says the word for abuse loses its final letter

parts.note: to insult someone is to abuse them verbally
in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

explanation.surface: Trendy slang is almost entirely rude, says a commentator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly all' cuts the last letter from INSULT, leaving INSUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulin is the pancreatic hormone that regulates blood sugar.

clue.text: You won't be out of pocket after this accident

definitions.text: You won't be out of pocket after this accident

parts.words: You won't be out of pocket after this accident
parts.note: in billiards or snooker, an accidental shot that sends the cue ball into a pocket after striking another ball leaves you in the pocket, not out of it

explanation.surface: An insurance mishap that costs you nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of pocket' suggests money lost; in billiards it is literal, and this shot ends with the ball down a pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-off is a billiards or snooker stroke where the cue ball rebounds off another ball into a pocket.

clue.text: One may be in a silly position to take chances

definitions.text: One may be in a silly position to take chances

parts.words: One may be in a silly position to take chances
parts.note: in cricket the silly positions are close fielding spots near the batsman, where catches (chances) come

explanation.surface: A reckless gambler puts themselves in a foolish spot.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, silly point and silly mid-on are fielding positions very close to the batsman; a 'chance' is a catching opportunity.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket fielder placed close to the wicket stands in the inner field, ready for catches.

clue.text: Drink offered by Soviet statesman having inflammatory impact

definitions.text: Drink offered by Soviet statesman having inflammatory impact

parts.words: Drink offered by Soviet statesman having inflammatory impact
parts.note: a mixed drink named after Vyacheslav Molotov, Soviet foreign minister, that is really a petrol bomb

explanation.surface: A Kremlin minister serves guests a fiery cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottle of petrol with a burning rag is a crude firebomb, named after the Soviet foreign minister.

clue.text: Copies some of the main points on a page

indicators.note: on places the compass points after a page, in an across clue meaning they follow it

parts.note: E and S, east and south, are two of the main compass points

explanation.surface: Someone summarises the key ideas on a sheet of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main points' are compass points here, not key ideas; two of them, E and S, follow A and P.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to mimic them, so it shares a verb sense with copying.

clue.text: Singer not getting on with instrument wedding guest heard

indicators.note: not getting says the word that follows is removed from the instrument

parts.note: in Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner the Wedding-Guest 'heard the loud bassoon'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vocalist who cannot get along with the wedding band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heard' is no sound signal: it recalls Coleridge's poem, where the Wedding-Guest hears the loud bassoon. Remove ON from BASSOON.
explanation.definitionFit: A basso is a bass singer, the lowest male voice in a choir or opera.

clue.text: Hide in moorland

definitions.meaning: in northern England, high open hill country

explanation.surface: Someone takes cover out on the moors.
explanation.definitionFit: Fell is both an old word for an animal pelt and the northern English term for upland moor.

clue.text: Sort of road that can damage a trailer

indicators.note: to damage something is to wreck its form, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A rough road surface can harm a towed trailer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damage' rearranges A TRAILER.
explanation.definitionFit: An arterial road is a main route carrying through traffic, like an artery carrying blood.

clue.text: Fast that is moved for a festival

indicators.note: something moved is shifted out of place, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: ie, id est, is Latin for 'that is'

explanation.surface: A day of fasting is rescheduled to make room for a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' rearranges FAST with IE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiesta is a Spanish or Latin American holiday celebration.

clue.text: Party policies needed to get people on board

definitions.text: needed to get people on board
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the boarding ramps themselves

parts.note: a gang is a group or party of people
planks are the separate policies of a political platform

explanation.surface: A political party needs its manifesto to win supporters over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' and 'policies' point to politics and 'on board' to winning support; really these are ramps onto a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Boarding ramps let passengers walk from the quay onto a ship.

clue.text: Comprehensive sporting triumph in which one never loses the lead

definitions.text: Comprehensive sporting triumph in which one never loses the lead

parts.words: Comprehensive sporting triumph in which one never loses the lead
parts.note: winning every major title in a season, or in bridge taking every trick, so the winning side always leads to the next trick

explanation.surface: A dominant champion stays in front all the way.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, the player who wins a trick leads to the next, so taking all thirteen means never losing the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning all the major tournaments, or all thirteen tricks at bridge, is a total sweep.

clue.text: Complaint of the hot-headed

parts.note: an ailment that strikes people whose heads get literally too hot in the sun

explanation.surface: A grumble from the short-tempered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' is an illness, not a grievance, and 'hot-headed' is literal, not quick-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Too long in strong sunshine brings on this illness of overheating.

clue.text: Bird that's quickly dropped in America

definitions.meaning: a pigeon-like bird, symbol of peace
American past tense of 'dive', meaning plunged fast

explanation.surface: A bird that swooped down suddenly over the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans say 'dove' for 'dived', and the same spelling names a small pigeon.

clue.text: Doctor leaves Arctic region, taking fish

indicators.note: a doctor who leaves a place departs from it, so his letters are taken out

parts.note: tundra is the treeless plain of the Arctic

explanation.surface: A physician quits the far north, bringing a fish catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' removes DR from TUNDRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is a large ocean food fish, also called tunny.

clue.text: Wearisome place old actors went to, for a change

definitions.text: old actors went to, for a change
definitions.note: a phrase standing for a noun: the place where actors went to change costume

parts.note: something tiring is wearisome
room means space or place

explanation.surface: Worn-out performers sought somewhere new for variety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' suggests variety; it means changing clothes. 'Tire' is an old word for attire.
explanation.definitionFit: In Elizabethan theatres, the dressing area behind the stage was where players put on their attire.

clue.text: Cheese with a portion of apricot tart

indicators.note: portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Cheese served alongside a slice of apricot tart.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft Italian whey cheese often used in desserts.

clue.text: Stock title

definitions.meaning: the stock of a gun or tool is the part you hold
slang for a name or title someone goes by

explanation.surface: A heading in a shop's stock list.
explanation.definitionFit: The grip of a tool is its stock or haft; a nickname is also called by this word.

clue.text: Pick flower of a certain type

definitions.meaning: the pick of a group is its best members
the flower of a group is its finest
a typewriter typeface size with twelve characters to the inch

explanation.surface: Choose a flower of a particular variety.
explanation.definitionFit: The choicest members of a group, and also a small typewriter typeface size.

clue.text: Model exhibitions are staged here

parts.note: fashion models parade along raised runways at shows, not scale models in a gallery

explanation.surface: A venue for displays of model railways or ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model exhibitions' suggests shows of miniatures; the models are people on a runway.
explanation.definitionFit: Fashion shows use narrow raised runways for models to parade along.

clue.text: Own daughter embraced by a short child

indicators.note: embraced by says the daughter is held inside the letters that follow
short says the word for child loses its final letter

parts.note: a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A mother claims her daughter, hugged by a little one.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid printed ARMET, a helmet, which neither 'Own' nor the wordplay supports; 'short' trims the child and 'embraced by' puts the daughter inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up is to confess, and to admit a fault is to acknowledge it.

clue.text: Face being placed in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word for placed is read backwards

parts.note: laid means put down or placed

explanation.surface: Confronting the prospect of being pensioned off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retirement' turns LAID back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: The face of a clock or watch is its numbered dial.

clue.text: Fascinated by runs included in start of jazz piece

indicators.note: included in says the runs are placed inside the word for fascinated by

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on or fascinated by it
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An enthusiast is hooked on the opening riffs of a jazz number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included in' puts R inside INTO.
explanation.definitionFit: An introduction is the opening passage of a piece of music.

clue.text: Bird unable to fly has time to ditch

parts.note: the moa was a huge flightless bird of New Zealand

explanation.surface: A flightless bird has time to abandon something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditch' looks like a verb, to abandon; it is a noun, a defensive trench.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep water-filled trench around a castle is a defensive ditch.

clue.text: Having paint in mind, like artists?

parts.note: tempera is paint bound with egg yolk
mental means existing in the mind

explanation.surface: Painters always have their paint on their minds.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the stereotype of moody, volatile artists.
explanation.definitionFit: Artists are proverbially moody and volatile in disposition.
